args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in production (healthy=false, error rate 18%) in us-east, us-west and eu-west. The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Next steps: confirm the service has recovered and find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before trying to deploy it again.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident (INC-0001).

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, was failing health checks and had an 18% error rate.
- **Version chosen:** v2.3.0 is the latest release that was healthy in production. The build before v2.3.1 was a test version (v2.3.1-rc) that ran only in staging, not production, and was also unhealthy there, so I skipped it.
- **Result:** All three regions are now on v2.3.0. The health check passes and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure and the rollback, and lists next steps: confirm recovery and find out why v2.3.1 failed before deploying it again. Opening the incident paged the on-call engineer.

No approval was needed, because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
